replacements.text: The Homebrew bash hangs one hook test. The gates ran with the system bash first on PATH (the executable search path).
The code reviewers last judged commit e399db1d (the last commit reviewed for code). Four prose-only commits followed it.
27 raw answers test the written dispatch rules. They reside on the author's machine outside the repository.
Tests check that every reviewer slot has configured effort and tools.
Edit the configured effort and tools in contracts.json (the panel's configuration file).
Either a run that dies is retried outside the recovery sequence or the round never stops.
Configured effort and tools
contracts.json sets effort and tools for every reviewer slot. No reviewer gets a shell.
The prompt generator writes one diff file beside each prompt.
A run that died is retried one effort step lower. The next retry uses the other provider. The round halts when that attempt dies too.
Every reviewer slot has configured effort and tools. The round record carries those settings. A missing configuration refuses the round. No tool grant can write.
A reader holding only the written dispatch rules reaches the configured dispatch, the fallback reviewer slot and each recovery step.
The recovery sequence proceeds one effort step down, then to the other provider, then to a halt. A claim outside that sequence is refused at no cost.
A live round runs every reviewer on the routing table's model at its configured effort and tools across two vendors.

Review cost and coverage were unpredictable. The agent running a review round chose each reviewer's effort and tool access itself. It avoided one model for whole-document reads on a belief unsupported by any run record.

The panel's configuration and each round's record hold the effort and tools configured for every reviewer slot. Every reviewer receives the change as a diff file. A run that dies mid-reasoning follows a recovery sequence of one effort step lower, then the other provider, then a round halt. Models still come from the shared routing table.

make ci, doc-lint and content-lint exit 0 at 5bc9e856 (the verified commit). 27 of 27 isolated reads of the written dispatch rules matched the expected answers. Code and prose review rounds both ended with no blocking findings. The gate does not yet check a run used its configured effort.

test_a17_a_dead_run_past_the_bound_is_out_of_attempts_not_off_ladder (the test for a dead-run claim past the attempt limit) failed before the change. It passes after the change. Restoring the old unconditional refusal makes only that test fail.
The design deletes the scope-keyed tier rule and tests challenged by this finding. The tier rule on main stands unchanged.

The verdict schema remains unchanged in this pull request as part of another skill outside this change. The notes on agents-config-9k9.408 (predictable reviewer settings, as an interim cost control) carry the missing halt reason for a follow-on item.
The advisory finding does not block. The schema is not edited. It still reads transport-failure for a halt caused by runs that died.

test_a17_a_dead_run_on_the_failover_seat_halts_after_an_earlier_unusable_output (the test for halting after a fallback run dies despite earlier unusable output) failed before the change with no halt key in the refusal. It passes after the change. Restoring the old check of every failure makes only that test fail.

219 emitter tests had passed with a mutant that dispatched every reviewer at its declared tier during a full reread. That mutant now fails this test for the prose, spec and typed-code full rereads. The branch passes it.

27 scenario reads were repeated on isolated readers with access only to copies of the five named files. The scenario file now identifies that reader and the reason an Agent-tool subagent does not qualify.

An isolation trial showed no instruction file visible to the isolated reader. The trial showed global instruction files visible to a reader with default settings. 27 of 27 isolated reads gave the expected answer. No unit test exercises an evaluation of the written dispatch rules.
change_diffs (the diff-generation function) now supplies every reviewer sharing a revision pair with bytes computed once for each distinct start revision.

five git diff calls were counted in an instrumented run for one typed-code emission. test_a18_lenses_sharing_a_revision_pair_share_one_diff (the test for sharing a computed diff) failed before the change. It passes after the change. The file-content, empty-change and unknown-revision tests still pass.

The example uses the OpenRouter frontier fallback slot for a whole-document read. contracts.json (the panel's configuration file) pins it at low effort. test_a6_every_lens_pin_has_its_stated_effort (the configured-effort test) holds that value. No test runs an example command. The example was read against the pin.

harvest.md now identifies only an `attempts-exhausted` refusal as ending a reviewer's run. A claim refused as `off-ladder`, or for a missing or malformed flag, remains correctable and claimable again at no attempt cost.

The gate raises those refusals before writing the ledger. They spend no attempt. test_a_refused_claim_rewrites_nothing_and_grants_no_attempt (the test for refusal without a ledger write or attempt) holds that behaviour.
harvest.md now identifies an attempt killed by the watchdog for silence as a run that died without output. The gate's no-output message names `dead-run` for that case and `transport-error` otherwise.

test_a_claimed_path_holding_no_file_is_a_transport_failure (the missing-output test) gained an assertion that the message names `dead-run`. The test failed before the change. It passes after the change.
No test exercises a comment. Both texts were read against the written dispatch rules. They describe only the fallback reviewer slot fixed by the routing table. harvest.md requires that recovery.

No test exercises a docstring. It was read against the code it describes. It states the rule held by test_a17_a_dead_run_on_the_failover_seat_halts_after_an_earlier_unusable_output (the test for halting after a fallback run dies despite earlier unusable output) in dispatch_gate_test.py.

The gate now restricts accepted recovery claims to failover onto the other provider of the Codex and OpenRouter pair or a lower-effort retry on the starting transport. A claim on any third transport is refused at no attempt cost.

test_a17_a_transport_that_is_not_the_failover_seat_is_refused (the test for refusing an invalid fallback transport) failed before the change because of gate authorisation of the claim. It passes after the change. A mutant that drops the same-transport guard from the lower-effort branch also fails it.
two starting-transport cases failed against the reviewer's mutant. The other two cases passed against that mutant. All four cases pass against the unchanged gate.

The gate attaches halt guidance only to an `attempts-exhausted` refusal. It raises an `off-ladder` refusal without halt guidance. No test exercises prose. The sentences were checked against that code.

The new sentences restate the gate's own no-output message. They agree with the section on runs that died. No test exercises prose. Another reviewer reported the same defect. This one change answers both findings.
The finding was advisory. It was fixed because the fix is cheap and right. The keyed answers did not change. No test exercises prose.

questions.question: Please add a separate Heads-up row for the unchecked use of pinned effort. The caveat must also remain in the summary.
The closing [9k9.408] must stay unchanged, but its first use needs a parenthetical gloss. May the title add the work item's meaning before that closing identifier?
The subject needs a parenthetical gloss for [9k9.408] while preserving its closing position and the 100-character cap. May its wording be shortened to make room for the work item's meaning?

Which files does 'only those files' name in the scenario paragraph, and what do 'staffing recommender', 'trend checkpoint', 'frontier', 'mid', 'artifact class' and 'criteria attack panel' mean? The record does not supply enough definitions for a faithful standalone rewrite of this section.
What do the roster's 'tier' and a reviewer's 'pin' mean here? The test name can be glossed as the round-record pin test, but the record does not define the tier categories.

What does check_route check? Its meaning is needed for the first-use gloss. Please also allow more than two sentences or approve a single description covering the comment and docstring without losing either assertion.
What failures does ROUTE_FAILURES list? The record names transport errors and dead runs elsewhere, but does not explicitly define this identifier.
What does exhausted() do? Its first-use gloss needs an explicit meaning.

This section independently asserts the unchanged off-ladder sentence, one sentence per case and no overlap, in addition to the halt-guidance change. May the two-sentence cap be relaxed so these claims can be separated faithfully?

Separating the independent claims gives 'No test exercises prose. Another reviewer reported the same defect. One change answers both findings.' Together with the unchanged change text, this reply has fewer than 40 words. May the minimum be relaxed rather than adding unsupported content?
Separating the transport rule, its reason and the removed outage narrative requires three sentences. May the two-sentence cap be relaxed, or may one of those claims move to another section?
